title: Introduction to gridmicrotex
text: gridmicrotex renders LaTeX math equations native R grid graphics objects (grobs). uses MicroTeX C++ library layout engine — MicroTeX parses LaTeX, builds TeX box model, computes exact glyph coordinates. package intercepts layout data maps native grid primitives (pathGrob, segmentsGrob, rectGrob, textGrob), producing gTree works R graphics device resolution. Key features: external LaTeX installation required — MicroTeX fully embedded Resolution-independent vector output R devices (PNG, PDF, SVG, …) Full math support: fractions, roots, integrals, matrices, Greek letters, accents, delimiters, Two bundled math fonts: Lete Sans Math (sans-serif, default) STIX Two Math (serif); additional fonts via load_math_font() Color support via \textcolor{} ggplot2 integration geom_latex() element_latex() CJK multilingual text \text{} blocks Markdown rendering inline math, via markdown_grob() markdown_box_grob() — see vignette("markdown")

title: Introduction to gridmicrotex
text: \mark{name} macro records named anchor inside formula, grobMark() resolves pair grid units ready drive arrow callout. Marks work nesting level — even inside superscript fraction — inherit surrounding transform (font shrink, scaling, rotation), anchor lands rendered glyph.  returned units carry grob’s viewport position hjust/vjust, go straight grid drawing function offset arithmetic. mark single point, span: centre callout multi-glyph term, use pair (\mark{l}…\mark{r}) take midpoint.
code: g <- latex_grob(   r"($a^2 + b\mark{term}^2 \mark{equals}= c^2$)",   x = 0.5, y = 0.4,   gp = grid::gpar(fontsize = 28) ) grid::grid.newpage() grid::grid.draw(g)  # Callout 1: the "=" sign, pointed at from above. mk_eq <- grobMark(g, "equals") grid::grid.segments(mk_eq$x, mk_eq$y + unit(15, "mm"),                     mk_eq$x, mk_eq$y + unit(3, "mm"),                     arrow = grid::arrow(length = unit(2, "mm"), type = "closed"),                     gp = grid::gpar(col = "red")) grid::grid.text("equals", x = mk_eq$x, y = mk_eq$y + unit(18, "mm"),                 gp = grid::gpar(col = "red", fontsize = 11))  # Callout 2: the b^2 term, pointed at from below — the mark sits at the # end of the term, including the superscript's smaller scale. mk_bsq <- grobMark(g, "term") grid::grid.segments(mk_bsq$x - unit(6, "mm"), mk_bsq$y - unit(15, "mm"),                     mk_bsq$x - unit(2, "mm"), mk_bsq$y - unit(3, "mm"),                     arrow = grid::arrow(length = unit(2, "mm"), type = "closed"),                     gp = grid::gpar(col = "blue")) grid::grid.text("b² term",                 x = mk_bsq$x - unit(7, "mm"),                 y = mk_bsq$y - unit(18, "mm"),                 just = "right",                 gp = grid::gpar(col = "blue", fontsize = 11))

title: Using LaTeX Math in ggplot2
text: common use case annotating regression fit model equation. Use annotate("latex", ...) single annotations — delegates GeomLatex internally avoids creating data frame automatically hides legend.
code: fit <- lm(mpg ~ wt, data = mtcars) b0 <- round(coef(fit)[1], 1) b1 <- round(coef(fit)[2], 1) r2 <- round(summary(fit)$r.squared, 3)  eq_label <- sprintf("$\\hat{y} = %s %s x, \\quad R^2 = %s$",                      b0, b1, r2)  ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg)) +   geom_point() +   geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +   annotate("latex", x = 4, y = 30, label = eq_label, size = 12) +   theme_minimal() #> `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'
